A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FINDAP/Llama-Fin study. The main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Llama-Fin benchmark results in Tables 2–5 and post-training ablation results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds original contamination analysis and metric reevaluations in Appendices A and F.

M1.justification: The joint CPT+IT recipe followed by FAP/SCP preference alignment, including DPO with an additional negative log-likelihood term, is retained. Added GenRM and attention-mask details document the implementation without establishing an algorithm or model change.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation dataset membership remains unchanged in Tables D.1, D.2, and E.1. Aqua remains listed despite its removed prose example. The added older-model comparison reuses FPB, FiQA SA, and NER; the contamination analysis uses existing FinTrain and FinEval data.

E2.justification: New Table F.1 adds comparisons with published scores for BloombergGPT, FinPythia 7B, and FinMA 7B/30B on three existing benchmarks. Main-table baselines remain unchanged. The outcome-only PA comparator shown in v2 Figure B.7 disappears.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 revises the stated CPT corpus from approximately 8B to 6B tokens without establishing retraining. Appendix F adds F1 and Entity F1 reevaluations on unchanged test samples, comparing zero-shot Llama-Fin with published few-shot results. Appendix A introduces exact matching and 10-gram screening followed by a greater-than-50% character-overlap check.

E4.justification: v3 adds a train–test contamination audit with manual inspection, but removes v2 Figure B.7, the only direct ablation isolating the added process-supervision component from outcome-only PA. This materially changes support for a central methodological contribution. The separate PA-In versus PA-Mix analysis survives as renumbered Figure B.7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Added results continue to use point estimates; contamination percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and retained ablation plots preserve their results. New Table F.1 reports Llama-Fin F1 scores of 91.28 for FPB and 95.39 for FiQA SA, and NER Entity F1 of 77.09; these are additional metrics, not performance gains over earlier metrics. Appendix A adds 0% exact and 0.003% fuzzy overlap rates. Results unique to removed Figure B.7 disappear.

T1.justification: No substantive mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The new overlap-checking criteria concern empirical evaluation procedures.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same framework, preference-alignment novelty, and Llama-Fin performance/generalization claims. The contribution list moves from v2 Appendix A into the introduction without changing its substantive scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix A interprets flagged overlaps as shared prompt formats or partial transcript content with unseen questions and answers, arguing against benchmark leakage. Existing explanations of forgetting, generalization, and reasoning tradeoffs, together with Section 6 limitations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies GPT-4o as GenRM, adds PA attention-mask details in Table G.1, and removes a duplicated scoring instruction from Figure D.1. It updates project/code/data access links and adds an 'upon acceptance' release statement. These disclosures do not establish changed implementation or actual resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds the FineWeb citation to Penedo et al. (2024), simplifies prior models' evaluation descriptions in Table 1, and expands discussion of older financial LLM comparisons. The main positioning against finance adaptation and reasoning-alignment research remains intact.

P1.justification: The contribution list moves into the introduction, new appendices cover contamination and older baselines, and the final recipe/prompt appendices are renumbered. Local copyediting, explanatory refinements, and corrected table-row references leave most prose and the overall narrative intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are reformatted, with Figure 2's reasoning paths simplified. v2 Figure B.7 is removed, the former B.8 is relocated and renumbered, and an older-baseline table is added. Captions and the recipe table receive local revisions; most displays retain their designs.

improvement.justification: The contamination audit and implementation disclosures improve validation and reproducibility, while Appendix F adds comparisons with aligned metrics but differing zero-/few-shot settings. However, removing v2 Figure B.7 eliminates the only direct ablation isolating process supervision, a central novelty. With the main results unchanged, these competing gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
